text: The shoe that fits one person pinches another; there is no recipe for living that suits all cases.
source: C.G. Jung, “The Aims of Psychotherapy,” Modern Man in Search of a Soul (1933), p. 69.

text: We cannot change anything unless we accept it.
source: C.G. Jung, “Psychotherapists or the Clergy,” Psychology and Religion: West and East, Collected Works 11, §520.

text: One does not become enlightened by imagining figures of light, but by making the darkness conscious.
source: C.G. Jung, “The Philosophical Tree,” Collected Works 13, §335.

text: No tree, it is said, can grow to heaven unless its roots reach down to hell.
source: C.G. Jung, Aion: Researches into the Phenomenology of the Self, Collected Works 9ii (1951), p. 43.

text: In all chaos there is a cosmos, in all disorder a secret order.
source: C.G. Jung, “The Archetypes and the Collective Unconscious,” Collected Works 9i, §66.

text: Everything that irritates us about others can lead us to an understanding of ourselves.
source: C.G. Jung, Memories, Dreams, Reflections, ch. IX, “Travels,” p. 247.
